citation: Crisostomo R. (2022) Measuring Transition Risk in Investment Funds. arXiv:2210.15329

dedupe_keys.name: framework for measuring climate transition risk in investment funds crisostomo 2022

description: This framework measures how a low-carbon transition would hit investment portfolios, using geographical, sectoral, company and ISIN-level data and distinguishing instruments by the carbon footprint of the counterparty and by credit rating, duration, convexity and volatility. Applied to a fund sector, it finds a moderate average loss of 5.7% if a high transition risk scenario materialises, but a strongly left-skewed distribution in which the worst 1% of funds lose 21.3% on average; equities lose most (12.7%), followed by corporate bonds (5.6%) and government bonds (4.8%), while sustainable funds are less exposed. It was developed by Ricardo Crisostomo and posted on arXiv on 27 October 2022 as a 25-page paper. Coverage follows the fund data used, which the abstract does not name. The preprint is available free online; only the arXiv licence link is shown and no code is linked. Caveats: it is a single-scenario analysis, and holdings data are not released. For simulation it provides a way to turn transition scenarios into losses for funds that finance industry, useful for feedback between climate policy, capital costs and industrial investment. It is related to the ECB investment fund network contagion climate stress test record in this catalogue.
